checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is p256verify input validation performed in the exact specified sequential order across all clients?

reachability.notes: Different validation orderings between clients cause consensus splits for edge-case inputs.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all Ethereum client implementations of the p256verify precompile. 2. For each client, trace the validation code path and document the exact order of validation steps. 3. Verify validation order matches specification: (a) length check (160 bytes), (b) r bounds [1, n-1], (c) s bounds [1, n-1], (d) qx bounds [0, p-1], (e) qy bounds [0, p-1], (f) curve equation check, (g) infinity check. 4. Craft edge-case inputs that would fail at different validation steps (e.g., input with invalid length AND invalid r value). 5. Submit identical edge-case transactions to multiple clients and compare results. 6. Document any divergence in return values or gas consumption between clients.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0050, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-003. Pre-condition property requiring strict validation ordering to prevent consensus splits.

checklist.title: Falsify Pre-condition: Can p256verify be invoked with inputs that bypass or reorder validation steps?

reachability.notes: Different validation orderings between clients cause consensus splits for edge-case inputs.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Generate test vectors for each validation step boundary: (a) 159-byte and 161-byte inputs, (b) r=0 and r=n inputs, (c) s=0 and s=n inputs, (d) qx=p input, (e) qy=p input, (f) point not on curve, (g) point at infinity. 2. For inputs failing multiple validation criteria, verify the FIRST failing check determines the result. 3. Compare gas consumed for inputs failing at step 1 vs step 7 - earlier failures should consume less gas. 4. Test combined invalid inputs (e.g., wrong length + invalid r) to confirm order-dependent behavior. 5. Verify no early-exit optimizations change the observable behavior across clients.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0050. Supporting check for validation ordering invariant. Edge cases with multiple invalid fields are highest risk for consensus splits.

checklist.title: Verify Actor Boundary: Does EVM caller to precompile transition enforce complete input validation before cryptographic operations?

reachability.notes: Different validation orderings between clients cause consensus splits for edge-case inputs.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review precompile entry point for actor-evm-caller to actor-precompile transition. 2. Verify all 7 validation steps complete BEFORE any signature verification computation begins. 3. Check for lazy evaluation or deferred validation that could allow partial processing. 4. Ensure validation errors return consistent error codes/gas costs across all clients. 5. Verify actor-evm-runtime correctly handles precompile return values for both success and validation failure cases. 6. Test that reverted transactions due to validation failures produce identical state roots across clients.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0050. Covers edges tb-001 (caller to precompile) and tb-003 (precompile to runtime). Untrusted transaction data must be fully validated before crossing into cryptographic processing.
